statement: Annual global averages: a standard offset of 0.88 °C is added to the annual ERA5 anomaly with respect to 1991-2020 to express it relative to 1850-1900 (multi-dataset estimate).
Human-induced warming reached 1.37 °C relative to 1850-1900 in 2025, increasing at 0.27 [0.2-0.4] °C per decade over 2016-2025.
Land covers about 29% of Earth's surface (oceans about 71%).
Land will continue to warm more than the ocean surface, likely 1.4 to 1.7 times more. We use the middle, 1.5, for the central line.

Each 1000 GtCO2 of cumulative CO2 emissions is assessed to likely cause a 0.27 °C to 0.63 °C increase in global surface temperature, best estimate 0.45 °C; reaching net zero CO2 is a requirement to stabilise warming.
